candidates.explanation: Labels behavior is scattered across domain, use-cases, adapters, DAL, UI, and infrastructure rather than colocated under one capability root. It adds a speculative repository port and separate forwarding use cases, including one wrapper per operation. Its RSC/GET/Server Action channels, server-derived authorization, private row mapping, and client/server separation are otherwise coherent.

The feature-oriented labels module and route-private app glue are clear, and it avoids a generic provider port. The service adds some ownership and normalization behavior but still introduces extra CRUD indirection. Channel selection and authorization are strong. Mapping is conceptually private, but the mapper is not explicitly server-only. The generic lib bucket violates the rubric.

The proposal correctly avoids a repository port and forwarding use-case layer, uses the required runtime channels, derives authority server-side, and confines provider mapping. However, labels behavior is distributed across multiple technical roots rather than one labels root. Separate per-operation inbound action wrappers and the repository-wide universal boundary/result normalization violate the negative criteria.

All capability behavior is colocated under modules/labels while route-specific composition stays under app. The concrete Supabase store has no speculative port or forwarding application-operation layer; the service owns meaningful failure translation. RSC reads, browser GET reads, and top-level Server Actions are correctly separated. Authentication, scoped authorization, private row mapping, caching, and failure ownership are all explicit without any listed negative pattern.
